question.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+4>6 \\ 4-x\ge 2\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $k$ that satisfy both $2x+4>6$ and $4-x\ge 2$ simultaneously.

- First, we solve $2x+4>6:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+4 & >6 \\ 2x+4-4 & >6-4 \\ 2x & >2 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & >\frac{2}{2} \\ x & >1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/6d3b61147527a632ccb46629a356e9f5c92a1ddfc8a52f3d0890cd46eb56f564.png)

- Then, we solve $4-x\ge 2:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}4-x & \ge 2 \\ 4-x-4 & \ge 2-4 \\ -x & \ge -2 \\ (-1)\cdot (-x) & \le (-1)\cdot (-2) \\ x & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/1452391c950b051c4cf454723498e6fa657f6d5f1315f78e50f3450bf7fbc1eb.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/a22a207cc64d33470e27d0b1f45ad0b87106fafd67b88c2163524a44951639bf.png)

    

Thus, the final solution is $x\in (1,2].$
